title: Olympia: the first Games

lines.text: Hi! This is a MyCast demo, and we are in Olympia, where the Olympic Games were born.
Tradition dates the first Games to 776 BC. They were held at a sanctuary in honour of Zeus every four years.
And that four-year cycle became a way to measure time, right?
Yes, the Olympiad became a unit of dating. Years were even named after the winner of the stadion, a sprint the length of the stadium.
What did the winner get? A gold medal?
No, a wreath of olive leaves. But the fame was huge: victors were honoured and their names recorded for later generations.
How did people travel to the Games if their cities were at war?
A truce, the ekecheiria, was announced for the Games, so athletes and pilgrims could reach Olympia safely.
For a long time only freeborn Greek men. But there were women victors too, as owners of chariots in the races.
Clever. What else was at Olympia?
The statue of Zeus, counted among the seven wonders of the ancient world. The last recorded Games were held in AD 393, under Emperor Theodosius.
So the Games ran for more than a thousand years. Amazing.
That was a MyCast demo episode. You can build your own podcast at mycast.pro.
